items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: So he gave Harlan notice and come on with the big band, you know.

ctx.x: See, and the big band, you know, and they can't be very old, and so Bird come up after we got through and said, 'Man, I want to play with you cats.' I said, 'Well, man, you know, you're with Harlan. You know Harlan ain't about to let you go.' He said, 'Well, man, I'll leave the band.' I said, 'Well, you got to give them some kind of notice or something.' He said, 'Well, okay, I'll give notice. I'll give him two week notice -- I'll give him a week.' I said, 'Give him two weeks' notice and take your time and come…

Now, during that time, see, that's the reason I say he had broke his habit, because he would take the reed, see, and I'd as point him, you know, to rehearse the reed section, because we would have section rehearsals. The brass would be over here rehearsing. The reeds would be over here. Bones over there, rhythm section over here, different parts of the hall, you know, whatever, you know. And then we'd bring the whole thing together, you know. And Bird used to keep right on and he'd keep right on them cats, you…

items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Yes, yes, the Bird was there. He’s the one who wanted to get in the book so fast.

ctx.x: Was Charlie Parker on that particular group?
Um humm. Yes, yes, the Bird was there. He’s the one who wanted to get in the book so fast.
He wanted to show him something, huh? Was it shortly after that that you did a radio broadcast with him and opened it up with “Cherokee?”
